title: Snow Mountain Hiker at Sunrise
description: Adventure photography style of a solo hiker on a snow-capped peak. Strong fit for outdoor brand marketing, REI-style blog content, and travel magazines.

prompt.main: lone hiker in red down jacket standing on a snow-covered mountain ridge at sunrise, vast alpine valley below filled with golden hour mist, jagged snow-capped peaks in the distance, dramatic clouds catching first light, patagonia advertising photography, canon EF 70-200mm f/2.8 --ar 16:9 --v 6.1 --s 500
prompt.negative: --no cartoon, flat illustration, indoor, sunny beach

explained.why: Patagonia/National Geographic ad ratio. Widescreen for landscape scale.
Mid stylize for documentary-but-beautiful. Higher stylize loses the "real photo" feel.

tutorial.intro: Adventure photography works because of scale contrast. Tiny human + vast landscape = emotional impact.
steps: Human subject: lone hiker in red down jacket 鈥?red jacket is the visual anchor in a white/blue scene.
Position: standing on a snow-covered mountain ridge 鈥?peak position = achievement.
Mid-ground: vast alpine valley below filled with golden hour mist 鈥?mist adds depth.
Background: jagged snow-capped peaks in the distance 鈥?multiple ridge layers create scale.
Light + camera: dramatic clouds catching first light, canon EF 70-200mm f/2.8 鈥?light + real lens name.
tutorial.tips: Red jacket + white snow is the classic adventure photo color combo. Without red, the hiker disappears into the scene.

faq.q: Why does my hiker look like a plastic figure?
faq.a: You forgot scale cues. "Vast alpine valley below" + "tiny human" makes the figure feel real in the landscape.

faq.q: How to get the Patagonia look?
faq.a: Add "patagonia advertising photography" + "canon EF 70-200mm f/2.8". Brand + lens = authentic outdoor aesthetic.
16:9 ratio with red jacket + golden hour. Reads instantly as "adventure".
